items.prompt: Repaint Image1 NovelAI storyboard as 黑暗形态, starring Chang Wuyu. Image1 locks three-quarter turning/back pose, face looking back over shoulder, one gloved arm raised, another near waist, cloak unfolding across right side, body continuous beyond lower crop. Image2 is EXCLUSIVE male identity: refined YOUNG ADULT MAN, restrained golden eyes/thin round glasses/pointed ears, silver-gray low hair bun with long sidelocks, black bent-tip wide-brim hat/purple lining, black high-collar long robe with restrained gold trim, black gloves, white feather plus BLUE SAPPHIRE gold clasp at left chest. Do not copy Image2 standing hand-on-glasses pose or fireball, never feminize/age him. Image3 PAINT only: matte opaque grouped masses, broad economical directional swipes, handmade hard shadow edges, selective face/hand detail, no kneeling/chains/light opening copied. OWNER COLOR OVERRIDE: replace Image1 WHITE backdrop with a full-bleed OPPRESSIVE low-key abstract field of charcoal-gray, black-violet and desaturated dark mauve. All corners dark, no paper margins. Reduce bright purple saturation and large silk-like highlights in cloak. Keep enough subtle gray-violet separation between real robe and shadow so silhouette reads; face/golden eyes/silver hair are the concentrated pale accents, not a bright purple aura. Dark magic is his own shadow pulled over shoulder like a second cloak: a few enormous overlapping black curtain-shaped planes reveal thin dull pale gaps suggesting hidden choices, not literal doors/rooms, a second person, glowing cards or spark confetti. Keep original turning gesture and scale; refine raised glove to guide/shroud shadow instead of a new unrelated prop. Face fully readable in three-quarter, meaningful connected neck/shoulder/chest/waist. Broad hair locks/coat planes, sparse colored structural lines, quiet secondary surfaces. No glossy metallic cloth, fine strands/creases, facet mosaics, cinematic photoreal fog, oil ridges or all-over grain. Single square profession card, no text/frame/UI/watermark.
